name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
overview: A government-backed, renewable one-year life insurance scheme offering a life cover of Rs. 2 lakh at a low annual premium, available to individuals with a bank/post office account.
objectives: Provide affordable life insurance coverage to the masses
Improve insurance penetration among low-income groups
Offer a simple, renewable term insurance product

benefits.title: Life Cover
benefits.description: Rs. 2 lakh life insurance cover in case of death due to any reason

otherCriteria: Individuals with a savings bank/post office account who provide consent for auto-debit of premium

applicationProcess.description: Approach the bank/post office where the savings account is held
Submit consent form for auto-debit of annual premium
Coverage active from enrolment till the next renewal cycle
Renew annually before the due date

faqs.question: What is the premium amount?
faqs.answer: A nominal annual premium as notified by the government, auto-debited from the linked account.

faqs.question: What is the life cover amount?
faqs.answer: Rs. 2 lakh in case of death of the insured member.

name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
overview: A government-backed, renewable one-year accidental death and disability insurance scheme offering coverage at a very low annual premium to bank account holders.
objectives: Provide affordable accident insurance to the masses
Cover accidental death and permanent/partial disability
Improve insurance penetration among low-income groups

benefits.title: Accident Cover
benefits.description: Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability, and Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability

otherCriteria: Individuals with a savings bank/post office account who provide consent for auto-debit of premium

applicationProcess.description: Approach the bank/post office where the savings account is held
Submit consent form for auto-debit of annual premium
Coverage active from enrolment till the next renewal cycle
Renew annually before the due date

faqs.question: What is the annual premium?
faqs.answer: A nominal amount as notified by the government, auto-debited from the linked account.

name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme (ESIC)
overview: A self-financed social security and health insurance scheme for Indian workers in the organised sector, providing medical care, cash benefits and other social security benefits to employees and their dependents.
objectives: Provide medical care to insured employees and dependents
Offer cash benefits during sickness, maternity and disability
Provide dependent benefits in case of employment-related death

benefits.title: Medical Benefit
benefits.description: Comprehensive medical care for the insured person and family

benefits.title: Cash Benefits
benefits.description: Sickness, maternity, disability and dependent benefits as per contribution

otherCriteria: Employees earning wages up to the prescribed ceiling, working in covered establishments

applicationProcess.description: Employer registers the establishment and employees under ESIC
Employee and employer contribute a percentage of wages monthly
Insured person receives ESIC pehchan card
Avail medical and cash benefits at ESIC facilities

faqs.question: Who is covered under ESIC?
faqs.answer: Employees earning wages up to the notified ceiling in ESIC-covered establishments.

faqs.question: What benefits are provided?
faqs.answer: Medical care, sickness benefit, maternity benefit, disability benefit and dependent benefit.

name: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)

ministry.name: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

overview: A comprehensive medical care scheme for central government employees, pensioners and their dependents, providing outpatient and inpatient care through CGHS wellness centres and empanelled hospitals.
objectives: Provide comprehensive healthcare to central government employees and pensioners
Ensure access to a wide network of wellness centres and empanelled hospitals
Reduce out-of-pocket healthcare costs for beneficiaries

benefits.title: OPD and Inpatient Care
benefits.description: Access to outpatient consultation and hospitalisation at CGHS wellness centres and empanelled hospitals

benefits.title: Cashless Treatment for Pensioners
benefits.description: Cashless facility for CGHS pensioner beneficiaries at empanelled hospitals

otherCriteria: Serving/retired central government employees and their eligible dependents in covered cities

applicationProcess.description: Apply for CGHS card through the department/pension disbursing office
Receive CGHS card for access to wellness centres and hospitals

faqs.question: Who is eligible for CGHS?
faqs.answer: Central government employees, pensioners and their dependents in CGHS-covered cities.

faqs.question: Is CGHS available in all cities?
faqs.answer: It is available in select CGHS-covered cities across India.

name: Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS)

ministry.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
ministry.department: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

overview: A crop insurance scheme that provides insurance protection to farmers against adverse weather conditions such as rainfall deficit, temperature and humidity that are deemed to adversely affect crop production.
objectives: Provide insurance against adverse weather conditions affecting crops
Mitigate financial hardship caused by weather-induced crop loss
Stabilise farm income during extreme weather events

benefits.title: Weather-Indexed Payout
benefits.description: Claim payout based on weather parameter deviations recorded at reference weather stations, without the need for individual crop-cutting assessment

otherCriteria: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, both loanee and non-loanee, where WBCIS is implemented in place of PMFBY

applicationProcess.description: Apply through bank, insurance company or CSC before the cut-off date
Weather data assessed against reference stations
Payout credited automatically based on weather triggers

faqs.question: How is WBCIS different from PMFBY?
faqs.answer: WBCIS uses weather parameters as a proxy for crop loss instead of yield-based assessment.

faqs.question: Is this scheme available everywhere?
faqs.answer: It is implemented in select states/areas as notified in place of yield-based crop insurance.
